Subject: Quick ask - smoothing credits vs adding days to trial

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for last week's demo — the latency numbers looked promising. We got internal approval to extend the evaluation, but procurement wants something cleaner on the finance side rather than just adding more days. Two asks from my CFO:

1) Can you convert unused trial days into a small pool of credits we can use for spike testing across regions (preferable)?
2) If credits are not possible, can you add a short 14-day grace window and lock pricing for any conversion to a committed plan for 60 days?

We want to avoid multiple invoices mid-eval. Attached is our short note on workloads and expected tokens. Can you flag any blockers on your side (legal, billing, or engineering)?

Best,
Emily Chen

+1 415-555-0123

Emily — really appreciate the clarity. Short answer: yes, we can do a credits option and we can also offer a short locked-price grace window. A couple of details so we can draft the right amendment: 

- Credits approach: we can convert up to 20% of remaining trial quota into a 200K-token credit pool that can be consumed on any region we support. Credits are non-refundable and expire 90 days after issue.
- Days (grace window) approach: we can add a 14-day runway and guarantee the conversion price for 60 days after the extended period. That would keep billing simple but does require a signed addendum.

I'll loop Kar and Steph for legal/billing and infra confirmation. Which of these does procurement prefer? If you want, we can put both options in an addendum and let them pick.

I attached a draft POC terms with both options — small changes from our standard POCA addendum.

—Priyom

Looping in from pricing/legal side — we have two viable plays here depending on risk appetite: 

Option A (credits):
- Convert up to 25% of remaining trial allocation to a token credit pool (we can make that 250K tokens for LumenAI).
- Credit expiry: 120 days to give them runway.
- Accounting note: we will issue a single credit memo; no incremental invoices for the trial period.

Option B (grace + price hold):
- 14-day extension of trial.
- 60-day price hold for conversion to a committed plan.
- We require a purchase order (PO) or signature on the addendum to lock the price; no retroactive credits.

One more concession we can offer to help conversion probability: a one-time 10% conversion discount if they sign within the 60-day hold and commit to a 12-month reserved capacity. That gives procurement a tangible incentive.

From infra/product: Stephanie confirms the credit pool across regions is feasible; engineering will tag credit usage to the LumenAI Org ID so usage is auditable.

If you want me to ok the final wording, I can sign off on the POC addendum today.

—Karthik
Head of Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference

Thanks Priyom/Karthik — this looks good. Procurement prefers Option A (credit pool) but asks that the credit expiration be 180 days instead of 120 to cover a longer validation window. They also asked whether the conversion discount could be structured as an earned rebate rather than an upfront discount (gives them better internal optics).

Two follow-ups from my CFO:
- Can the credit memo be issued with a reference to our PO number so it's easier to reconcile?
- If we go the rebate route, what trigger events would qualify (e.g., commit to 12 months at >= X tokens/month)?

We can sign the addendum once terms are in the document. Also happy to hop on a 20-minute call to finalize, if helpful.

Best,
Emily

- We will issue the credit memo referencing your PO number (please send the PO when you have it).
- Rebate structure suggestion: an earned rebate that converts to an invoice credit when LumenAI signs a 12-month reserved capacity at or above the agreed minimum committed throughput (we usually set that at 1M tokens/month for this tier). Next steps: I can update the POC addendum with Option A terms (250K token credit pool, 180-day expiry, credit memo with PO ref, and earned-rebate language). Do you want us to include the 10% earned rebate language in the same addendum or a separate conversion incentive addendum?
